text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Decide to auto-apply safe, low-risk improvements to our own codebase using PR-Agent. It scans pull requests for style, docs, and simple bugs, then suggests fixes we can merge with one click. This cuts review time for obvious issues and keeps the code clean without slowing down real work. The trade-off is trusting the tool’s judgment—we might miss edge cases it doesn’t flag, so we’ll keep human review for complex changes.

name: Gauge
text: PR-Agent’s auto-apply risks normalizing sloppy reviews—if the tool greenlights fixes without human eyes, we’ll miss context that matters for the feature, not just style. A safer path is to auto-apply *only* to our own self-improvement repo, where the stakes are low and we can iterate fast; anything touching customer-facing code still goes through a human. Settle it by running a 2-week pilot on the self-improvement repo and comparing pre/post review time and defect escape rates—if escape rates rise, we scrap the idea.

name: Sprocket
text:
Auto-apply safe style and doc fixes to *all* PRs via PR-Agent, but block merges if the PR-Agent score drops below 90%. This keeps the tool’s speed for obvious fixes while forcing humans to review anything it flags as risky. The trade-off is that we’ll still see some false positives—cleanup that matters but scores low—but we avoid missing real issues by trusting the tool only when it’s confident.

name: Gauge
text: PR-Agent’s 90% threshold is arbitrary—it doesn’t measure *which* risks matter, just how many. A safer rule: auto-apply only to files that have passed *human* review in the last 30 days, where we’ve already proven the context is stable. That settles it: no tool overrides fresh human judgment, and we keep the speed where it counts.

name: Ratchet
text: DECISION: Auto-apply PR-Agent style/doc fixes only to files with recent human approval (last 30 days), blocking merges if PR-Agent score drops below 90%. Result: Cleaner code without overriding fresh human context. Owner: Sprocket.
